messages:
sam: Heads-up — p99 on the latency dashboard for /v1/generate spiked around 09:10 after the proxy change.
anya: ugh, can you grab the chart or link?
sam: https://console.redwood.ai/dash/latency?endpoint=%2Fv1%2Fgenerate
sam: p50 steady, p95 small uptick, p99 huge jump in a few points at 09:10
chao: did we roll any routing/weight changes recently?
kevin: I rolled routing-policy-v2 at 09:05 to shift fallback weights for cheaper GPUs
sam: my hypothesis: quota or routing fallback bounced some traffic into slower pool, skewing tail
anya: are synthetic/perf jobs excluded from the SLO dashboard? last week we had sampling-origin tagging missing
sam: not for this view — rollups currently include everything by default
chao: observability-bot: annotate deploy routing-policy-v2 1778889990
observability-bot: deploy annotated: routing-policy-v2 @ 1778889990 (user: kevin)
kevin: quick question — how is p99 computed across routes? reservoir sampling is what we use afaik
anya: yes, we use reservoir over the ingestion window; that can bias if one route floods the sample
sam: perf-ci kicked off synthetic runs at 09:08, timeline matches
chao: if synthetic jobs come from a single client, and we don't stratify merge by client/route, p99 will reflect that
kevin: two short options: (A) filter out client=test by default in SLO dashboards, (B) change merge to be stratified by route/client
anya: (A) is easy and fast. (B) is more correct for mixed traffic but needs infra work
sam: did a quick query to validate:
```
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 99) AS p99
FROM requests
WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND NOT client='perf-ci'
GROUP BY floor(minute, 1)
ORDER BY minute DESC
LIMIT 60;
```
sam: excluding perf-ci brings p99 back to baseline
kevin: that proves it. So synthetic traffic is the primary contributor
anya: UX thing — console should show a small "sample-origin" pill in the legend (prod / synthetic / fallback) and let folks toggle
chao: agree. Also need to document whether percentiles are calculated on raw sample or reweighted merge — customers misinterpret otherwise
sam: thought: we should surface the sample composition % next to the percentile (e.g., prod: 80%, perf: 15%, fallback: 5%)
kevin: ops action: add alert that triggers when p99 delta > 40% and sample-origin composition shifts by > 10%
anya: and add a quick filter in the dashboard to exclude/include synthetic with one click
chao: longer term: implement stratified merging where we compute percentile per-stratum and then take weighted percentile to avoid single-stratum domination
sam: opened frontend PR for the pill + toggle: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1234
kevin: infra follow-up: can telemetry tag client=test earlier in pipeline? that will make filtering reliable
sam: tagging is possible; I'll file infra ticket and cc you
sam: @ingrid can you take a quick look at the PR and the alert suggestion when you have a minute? :pray:
ingrid: will review by EOD. tentatively +1 on pill and alert, need to sync on thresholds
anya: also add a note in dashboard docs explaining why p99 can move even when p50/p95 are stable (sampling bias explanation)
chao: noted — I'll draft a short blurb for docs
sam: thanks. once PR merges I'll update the dashboard and mute perf-ci from SLO views until we have stratified merging
kevin: follow-up doc for stratified merge design please, I'll own infra changes
sam: ok, created internal ticket INF-2045
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
